;Disasters and accidents
* [[Sudan Airways Flight 139]] crashes in [[Port Sudan]], killing 116 passengers. A toddler of two or three years is the sole survivor. [https://web.archive.org/web/20050427130903/http://asia.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=topNews&storyID=3052818 (Reuters)] [http://famulus.msnbc.com/FamulusIntl/ap07-10-122117.asp?reg=AFRICA (MSNBC)]{{Dead link|date=August 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}

;Health
* [[Ladan and Laleh Bijani]] die during their unsuccessful separation operation in [[Singapore]]. [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/asia-pacific/3055016.stm (BBC)]

;Law and crime
* A worker at a [[Lockheed Martin]] [[aircraft]] parts factory in [[Meridian, Mississippi]], shoots 13 co-workers, killing five, before committing [[suicide]]. Investigators are unsure of the motive. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A29480-2003Jul8.html (Washington Post)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120805115209/http://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/articles/A29480-2003Jul8.html |date=2012-08-05 }}

;Politics and elections
* During a visit to the former [[slavery|slave]]-trading station on [[Goree Island]], off the coast of [[Dakar]], [[Senegal]], [[President of the United States of America|U.S. President]] [[George W. Bush]] calls slavery "one of the greatest crimes of history", but stops short of an official apology. [https://web.archive.org/web/20050427130853/http://asia.reuters.com/newsArticle.jhtml?type=politicsNews&storyID=3054883 (Reuters)]
* [[Same-sex marriage in Canada]]: A [[British Columbia]] court rules that [[gay|same-sex]] couples may [[same-sex marriage|get married]] in that province, effective immediately. BC becomes the second Canadian province, and second political division in the Western Hemisphere, to legalize same-sex marriage. This decision is similar to the [[Ontario]] decision on [[June 2003|June 10, 2003]]. [https://archive.is/20030711150217/http://cnews.canoe.ca/CNEWS/Canada/2003/07/08/130210-cp.html (Canada News)]
